title: RTBF caseflow orchestrator with evidence snapshot retainer
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers need an auditable, legally defensible way for their Right-To-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) requests to be processed across Redwood's hosted and private deployments. Current deletion workflows are siloed per subsystem and do not provide a single, queryable artifact that preserves pre-deletion evidence (what data existed, processing lineage, and the retention policy that triggered deletion). This leads to lengthy compliance reviews and manual evidence collection for audits.

Goal: Implement a "Caseflow Orchestrator" that coordinates RTBF requests across services, captures immutable evidence snapshots at key lifecycle moments, retains those snapshots in an escrowed, region-aware store for configurable windows, and exposes an audit export that satisfies internal legal and customer requests. The feature should support: automated request adjudication (auto-confirm, needs-review, legal-hold), selective retention exemptions (legal hold, contract obligations), region-residency-aware execution, and an evidence snapshot retainer that signs and stores verifiable proof bundles while the underlying data is deleted per policy.

Success metrics: reduction in mean time to produce deletion evidence from 2 business days to under 4 hours for 90% of RTBF requests; automated handling of 70% of incoming RTBF requests without human review; and support for region-stamped audit bundles for EU/US residency boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: A request can be submitted via API/Console and assigned a unique case ID that routes to the orchestrator
Orchestrator can run adjudication rules: auto-confirm (no PII found), escalate (needs review), or apply legal hold exemptions

For any case marked for deletion, the system captures an evidence snapshot (metadata, hashes, retention policy, model/embedding references) before deletion and stores it in an escrow store with cryptographic signing
Evidence snapshots include region stamp and retention-policy version and are queryable by case ID for the configured retention window
Console exposes a per-case timeline with actions, status, and downloadable signed evidence bundle (JSON + checksum + signature)
Audit export supports bulk assembly of bundles for a tenant and produces a verifiable index for auditors
Automated test harness validates that deletion happened and that evidence bundles can be verified end-to-end with stored signatures
Fallback policy: if escrow store is unavailable, orchestrator pauses deletion and issues an alert to SRE and Compliance; this behavior is documented in runbook
implementation_notes: Orchestrator service sits in control plane and owns RTBF case lifecycle; interacts with data-plane delete APIs (hosted/dedicated/private)
Evidence snapshot retainer collects: pre-deletion object metadata, storage location pointers, model inference logs referencing user tokens, retention policy id, timestamps, and operator actions
Snapshots are serialized into a canonical JSON format and signed with KMS-backed key; signature metadata added to the bundle manifest
Escrow store is region-aware S3 buckets with lifecycle policies; for Private deployments use KMS + customer-managed storage connector (S3/GCS) if requested
Console work: new RTBF case view, bulk case exporter, per-tenant export permission, and indicators for legal-hold/exemption status
API changes: POST /rtbf-cases, PATCH /rtbf-cases/:id/actions (apply_hold, confirm_delete, cancel), GET /rtbf-cases/:id/evidence
Observability: per-case traces, SLOs for case adjudication time, metrics for snapshot size and escrow latency; add dashboards and alerting
Privacy: redact sensitive fields from evidence snapshot where storage of raw PII is forbidden; instead include hashes and a redaction manifest
Legal: provide retention-window configuration and an evidence-bundle TTL that is separate from deleted data retention (configurable per-tenant and region)
Security review: require threat model review for signed bundles and escrow access patterns; rotate signing keys quarterly
comments: 2026-03-02 - PM note: Initial scoping completed with legal and privacy. Legal prefers signed bundles over DB snapshots. Need SRE input on escrow durability and availability trade-offs.

2026-03-03 - Eng feedback (Diego Alvarez): Prefer implementing snapshot serializer as an independent library to avoid duplication across services. Will prototype signing + verification in go/crypto-lib.

2026-03-04 - Design feedback (Maya Li): Console case timeline needs compact view for high-volume tenants and export button only for users with 'compliance:export' permission. Added wireframes to Drive.
2026-03-04 - PM follow-up: Added dependency on PM-11822 for deletion confirmation API and on PM-25120 for proof API shape alignment. Also flagged for security review during Cycle 2026-W12.

2026-03-05 - SRE comment (Jamal Brooks): Escrow buckets will be single-region by default; recommend multi-region replication only for enterprise tenants due to cost. Will provide cost estimate next sync.
